questions.title: Explain React Reconciliation and the Virtual DOM.
questions.description:
Reconciliation and Virtual DOM

Reconciliation is the process through which React updates the real DOM. Instead of re-rendering everything, React maintains a virtual representation of the UI (the Virtual DOM) in memory.

When state or props change, React generates a new Virtual DOM tree and diffs it with the previous tree using a heuristic O(n) algorithm.

Heuristics

  • Different elements produce different trees.
  • The key prop helps identify which elements changed across renders, enabling item reordering rather than destruction/recreation.
questions.bestPractices:
• Always provide unique, stable keys for items in a list. Avoid using list indexes if items can reorder, insert, or delete.
  • Keep components small and state localized to minimize diffing subtree sizes.
questions.commonMistakes: • Using Math.random() or indices as keys, which ruins rendering performance and breaks component state when items move.
questions.example:
// GOOD: Stable ID as key
items.map(item => (
  <TodoItem key={item.id} todo={item} />
))

// BAD: Index as key (if list is dynamic)
items.map((item, index) => (
  <TodoItem key={index} todo={item} />
))
questions.interviewTip: Explain React Fiber briefly as the modern reconciler that allows splitting reconciliation work into chunks and pausing/prioritizing updates to keep the main thread responsive.
